title: Skip the Pricey Sweet Shops: Make Soft No-Cook Kaju-Pista Modak at Home
excerpt: No gas, no mava, no sugar syrup — this cashew-and-pistachio modak comes together in a mould in under 30 minutes, just in time for Ganeshotsav.
body:
• This Kaju-Pista Modak needs no gas, no mava and no sugar syrup — cashew and pistachio powders are kneaded into soft doughs with powdered sugar, milk powder, cardamom and a spoonful of milk.
  • Use a greased modak mould: line the outside with the cashew dough and fill the centre with the pistachio mixture for a striking two-tone sweet.
  • Grind the nuts separately in short pulses so they form a fine powder without releasing oil; add milk only a teaspoon at a time to keep the dough soft, not wet.
  • A festive alternative to expensive, adulteration-prone market mithai during Ganeshotsav, when modaks are offered to Bappa as the season's most beloved prasad.

During Ganeshotsav, no offering to Bappa feels quite complete without modak — and every year, the festive sweet shops cash in. Prices climb, and so does the worry about adulteration in store-bought mithai. The answer may already be in your kitchen: a soft, premium-tasting Kaju-Pista Modak made at home from nothing more than cashews, pistachios and a few pantry staples, without lighting the gas at all.

The velvety sweetness of cashew paired with the earthy aroma of pistachio melts in the mouth, and the no-cook method means there is no mava to reduce, no syrup to thread, and no risk of a burnt batch. It is the kind of sweet that looks patisserie-grade in a gift box but comes together in under half an hour.

Ingredients

For about 10–12 modaks:

"The answer may already be in your kitchen: a soft, premium-tasting Kaju-Pista Modak made at home from nothing more than cashews, pistachios and a few pantry staples, without lighting the gas at all."

  • Cashews — 1 cup
  • Pistachios — 1/2 cup
  • Powdered sugar or tagar — 3/4 cup
  • Milk powder — 2 tablespoons (for binding)
  • Green cardamom powder — 1/2 teaspoon
  • Milk — 2 to 3 teaspoons, as needed
  • Desi ghee — 1 teaspoon (for the mould)
  • Green food colour or a pinch of saffron — optional

Method

Step 1 — Grind the nuts. Put the cashews and pistachios in separate mixer jars and run the mixer in short bursts until each forms a fine powder. Do not grind continuously: the nuts will release oil and turn pasty instead of powdery.

Step 2 — Make the cashew dough. In a bowl, combine the cashew powder with half the powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon of milk powder, the cardamom powder and 1–2 teaspoons of milk. Knead gently with a light hand until it comes together as a soft, pliable dough.

Step 3 — Make the pistachio dough. In a second bowl, mix the pistachio powder with the remaining powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon of milk powder, the colour or saffron, and about 1 teaspoon of milk. Knead into a second soft dough.

Step 4 — Shape the modaks. You can simply mix the two doughs together for a marbled effect — or make the classic two-tone version: grease a modak mould lightly with ghee, press a little of the cashew mixture along the edges of the mould, fill the centre with the pistachio mixture, close the mould and press firmly. Open it to reveal a beautifully patterned, soft modak.

Why it works for the festive season

Market sweets during the festival rush are not only expensive; in recent years, food-safety crackdowns around festivals have repeatedly found suspect stock on shelves. A homemade modak sidesteps both problems at once — you control every ingredient, and the no-cook technique removes the most failure-prone part of traditional mithai-making.

The texture depends on two small disciplines: grind the nuts only to a fine powder (never to a paste), and add milk sparingly. Too much liquid and the dough turns sticky; the right amount leaves it soft enough to release cleanly from the mould with sharp ridges.

Serving and storage

Serve the modaks as prasad or pack them in a lined box for gifting — the cashew-outside, pistachio-inside version looks striking enough to pass for a premium mithai-shop creation. Because they contain fresh milk and no preservatives, refrigerate them and finish within two to three days. A pinch of saffron in the pistachio dough, instead of colour, gives a more natural tint and a gentle aroma that suits the festive table.

nri_angle: For diaspora families celebrating Ganeshotsav far from India's mithai shops, this no-cook modak delivers an authentic prasad with ingredients available at any international grocery store.
